column1: # Files this scaffold ONCE SHIPPED and no longer does.
# WHY A MANIFEST RATHER THAN A TREE DIFF (#253). scaffold_upgrade compares the adopter's
# BASELINE release against the NEW one to decide what upstream retired. That is sound for
# anything retired DURING the span being upgraded across, and structurally blind to anything
# retired BEFORE the baseline: such a file is in neither tree, so it cannot be told apart
# from one the adopter added. Measured -- an adopter on 0.38.3 upgrading to 0.82.2 still had
# both files below, because they were already gone from upstream when that baseline was cut.
# EVERY SHA THE PATH WAS EVER SHIPPED WITH, NOT JUST THE LAST (#255). A file changes over its
# shipped life. Recording only the final revision misclassifies every adopter sitting on an
# earlier one as having EDITED it -- and the adopters most likely to be on an older revision
# are the ones who have carried the file longest, which is exactly the backlog this manifest
# exists to clear. Measured: install_ollama_service.sh shipped in four distinct revisions; an
# adopter holding the 0.14.0 one was told they had edited a file they had never touched.
# Matching ANY shipped sha means "you never touched this" is answered correctly.
# LOCALCODER'S FILES CARRY A NOTE BEGINNING `localcoder:`. Until 0.36.0 (7b78042, W-15) the
# scaffold vendored localcoder's implementation into every adopter; an adopter that took an
# early release and upgraded since still carries every one of those files, untouched.
# scaffold_upgrade removes them like any other row EXCEPT in the repository that declares
# `<!-- scaffold:owns-localcoder -->`, where they are the product. That skip is not optional:
# the vendored copies were identical to the product's, so localcoder's own
# docs/benchmarks/reference/apple-m3-max.md still matches a shipped sha today.
# ai/eval_tasks.py IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. The split removed it from the scaffold, but the
# installed localcoder reads each project's own ai/eval_tasks.py (localcoder_eval.py), and
# the docs promise the file is "yours, never overwritten by an upgrade". It is an integration
# point, like ai/localcoder.config.json, not a leftover.
# FORMAT, tab-separated:   <path>   <comma-separated shas, any may match>   <note>
tools/install_ollama_service.sh
tools/com.ollama.serve.plist.template
docs/benchmarks/README.md
